wording.engine_summary: Boots an installed Windows 11 Arm desktop on BridgeVM's own Hypervisor.framework VMM with storage, display/input, network, audio, guest agent and experimental 3D. Not release-ready.
wording.machine_contract: QEMU virt-compatible guest contract with documented deviations

criteria.title: Cold boot reliability
criteria.statement: At least 9 of 10 cold boots report stage4_pass=1 AND firstboot_fresh=1 in firstboot-stage.txt.
criteria.measured: Eight instrumented 5-boot soaks (14/40 aggregate) with owning-thread GIC reads at every terminal stall. Two failure shapes fully characterized: UEFI (PPI pending at GICR, CPU interface open/idle, never taken) and kernel (CNTV_CTL ISTATUS=0 with CVAL millions of ticks past -- the fire never forms). Mechanism found for some UEFI stalls: stale running priority RPR=0x10/AP1R0 with ISACTIVER0=0 (swallowed trapped EOI); clearing it works (verified rpr->0xff) but delivery still does not resume. Every host lever tried and measured: unmask, CVAL rewrites, mask pulse, forced ISPENDR0 (delivers -- boot dies anyway; falsified as cure), ICC APR clear. ICH list registers unreadable (EL2 view unavailable). Defect isolated to Apple's in-kernel GICv3/vtimer under hv_vcpus_exit pressure; no public API re-arms forwarding. Apple Feedback draft ready (a1-apple-feedback-draft-20260806.md); remaining host option: relocate guest wake onto an owned device interrupt.

criteria.title: Vulkan title frame rate
criteria.statement: A real Vulkan title reports guest-side samples>0 AND p50>=30 FPS.
criteria.measured: Instrument repaired end to end 2026-08-06 (bd31835..2ab575d): frame-log read opens shared (title holds it open), cube.iso content ships through the share and is required (a menu emits no fps lines), fps lines need --loglevel=3, per-file sync waits survive the zip winning the scan order. Gate reached BVGPU-REAL-TITLE-PASS with venus_icd_loaded from the DriverStore on canonical-attach-resident-20260731 (net-live-20260724 unusable: viogpu3d CM_PROB_UNSIGNED_DRIVER). Five subsequent runs all wedged in the A1 interrupt-loss class before any fps line could exist (boot stalls; agent control channel lost after zip sync). Measurement formally queued behind A1 run stability. PresentMon remains structurally blind to this swapchain; the guest-side fps log is the A2 instrument.

criteria.title: D3D11 title frame rate
criteria.statement: A real D3D11 title reports guest-side samples>0 AND p50>=30 FPS.
criteria.measured: Instrumentation works with samples=311-369, but p50 is approximately 20 FPS. A self-authored D3D11 smoke reaches 54.3 FPS on the same path, so the stack is not capped at 20; the title stays on Composed: Flip and never reaches Hardware: Independent Flip.

criteria.measured: 1600x900, 1920x1080 and 1280x720 all PASS with a matching final SET_SCANOUT.

criteria.statement: The app in /Applications boots to 3D while the source repository is renamed away.
criteria.measured: Deep codesign plus bundled Hypervisor entitlement verified; booted with the repository renamed to bridgevm.a10-hidden; device_status=0xf, 3D commands=649, create3d=826, flush=533.

criteria.title: No regression
criteria.statement: Workspace, Venus lib, probe example and Swift suites plus fmt, clippy, budgets and docs gates all pass at the final release head.
criteria.measured: All 651 Swift XCTest functions now RUN under the shim via scripts/run-xctest-shim-suites.sh (BridgeVMApp 403, BridgeVMControl 185+1 skip, AppleVzRunnerCore 62; three per-suite runners, so the 58 redeclaration errors of a merged module never arise). Running found a drifted test compiling could not: the text-input test asserted pre-39a4f63 drop-non-ASCII behavior and crashed on lines[1]; fixed to the current contract. Falsified: hidChunkBytes 32->16 fails exactly that test. Caveat printed by the runner itself: measured under a shim, not Apple XCTest. Rust/fmt/clippy/budgets/docs all pass at current head. The criterion stays OPEN until re-established at the final V1 release head, which does not exist yet.

criteria.title: Secure SMCCC TRNG
criteria.statement: Guest TRNG_RND_32/64 are served only by the host OS CSPRNG; no exit-count, time, PID or constant-derived fallback exists, and provider failure returns NO_ENTROPY.
criteria.measured: The protocol lives in bridgevm_hvf::smccc_trng over SecRandomCopyBytes, with one dispatch shared by the primary and secondary loops. 17 tests cover the DEN 0098 register layout, bit masking, request limits, FEATURES discovery and the fail-closed paths; the exit-counter generator and the duplicated probe constants are deleted. Guest-visible behaviour is not yet re-measured on a live boot.

criteria.title: PSCI 1.1 conformance
criteria.statement: CPU_ON and AFFINITY_INFO implement the specified state table, affinity levels and error codes with atomic state transitions.
criteria.measured: State logic lives in bridgevm_hvf::psci with 19 tests covering the CPU_ON table, affinity levels 0-3, cluster aggregation, CPU0, RES1 spellings and invalid targets/levels. CPU_ON reports ON_PENDING for a pending CPU, AFFINITY_INFO reads X2 and searches the whole topology, and the state check and Off->OnPending transition share one critical section. Live 1/2/4-vCPU topology validation is not yet run.

criteria.title: Typed product runtime
criteria.statement: The product app and hvf-runner drive a typed runtime API from a versioned launch manifest instead of executing an example binary through shell.
criteria.measured: Twenty-four R1 slices (f545fd0..bfe5d72): bridgevm-hvf-runtime owns the product lifecycle (manifest validation, pre-launch writer leases, env_clear allowlist spawn with EXIT_ON_RESET baked in, run_vm with flush+receipt between generations, DeviceSurfaces mirroring the wrapper env byte-for-byte incl. virgl/1050 vs venus split, supervisor-owned swtpm with key-over-fd-0 encrypted state, watchdog-less app mode). The APP now launches through it: HvfEngineSession prefers the packaged hvf-runner --launch-spec (runnerArguments() vector pinned by the 188-test suite; wrapper stays as source-checkout fallback), and package-hvf-control-app.sh bundles hvf-runner. Proven live twice at the app vector: dev build and the PACKAGED BUNDLE's own binaries (hvf-runner + probe + firmware from BridgeVMControl.app/Contents/Resources) booted the canonical image -- virgl device 0x1050, BVAGENT READY, in-guest shutdown, PSCI SYSTEM_OFF, RUNNER-EXIT 0. OPEN only for a GUI-driven session run at the final V1 head (the code path is the one proven here).

criteria.title: Process-recreate reset
criteria.statement: 100 consecutive guest SYSTEM_RESETs each produce a new helper PID, an increasing reset generation, a fresh guest boot marker and 4 online CPUs.
criteria.measured: Process-recreate reset proven LIVE on BOTH paths. Harness (scripts/verify-reset-recreate.sh): 3/3 cycles -- fresh helper PID, increasing generation, that boot's own BVAGENT READY, 4 online CPUs answered by the guest, in-guest PSCI reset, exit 42 asserted; 10-cycle run added intermediate-reset semantics then ended in the A1 stall at cycle 3. Typed path (hvf-runner --launch-spec --helper --helper-agent-control): 4 generations live, 3 READY boots, 3 exit-42 recreations, generation-tagged receipts, stall correctly receipt-less (2a586c7 evidence addendum). OPEN: the gate is 100 consecutive cycles and the A1 stall class interrupts long chains until fixed -- endurance is A1-bound, not reset-path-bound.

criteria.title: Release security and storage hardening
criteria.statement: Release builds launch only bundled signed helpers, verify socket peer UID, hold an exclusive disk/vars lease and use positional atomic disk I/O.
criteria.measured: Overrides: scripts/check-release-overrides.sh inspects compiled objects and reports 4 overrides debug-only, PASS. Bundled signed helper: HelperCodeSignature.swift requires the swtpm helper to share the app team ID, with 10 swift-testing tests. Peer UID: crates/bridgevm-daemon/src/peer_credentials.rs with tests. Exclusive lease: crates/bridgevm-hvf/src/media_lock.rs. Positional atomic disk I/O: every seek+read on a data path is now read_exact_at/write_all_at -- nvme/disk.rs (read, write-back write, and the copy-on-write chunk fault), probe_mmio/virtio_backend.rs, virtio_blk/media_backend.rs and windows_arm/uefi_io.rs, whose write_all_at/read_exact_at were named for positional I/O while seeking. Three tests park the shared file offset at 4096, perform a read, a write-back write and an overlay fault, and require it to still be 4096; falsified by restoring seek+read, which reports the offset moved to 1536. The one remaining seek is in media_lock.rs, rewriting the lock file's holder line, which is not a data path.

criteria.title: Nonblocking provenance-sealed live queue
criteria.statement: Long gates run asynchronously on the Studio local queue with sealed commit/image/vars hashes and no foreground wait beyond 120 seconds.
criteria.measured: The Studio local queue (com.ketchio.bridgevm-live LaunchAgent, StartInterval 60s, no inbound listener and no runner registration) has run 29 jobs across tiers t0-t5 plus t1-snapshot and t1-restore-boot. Submission returns a job id immediately and never waits, so no foreground wait exists at all, let alone one over 120 seconds; the longest job this session ran about 100 minutes unattended. Receipts seal the commit and, for tiers that read one, the image and vars: job 20260805-115614-86173-14911 records image_sha256 6fef8f980adbc6af1ed41a1934d1ebafd93b8a1b4d2ab9a3f8bd07ae950d9b54 and vars_sha256 d329b5b03cc5673435d3949f1b5b5b2bfe3f4dfe1f6f0b56ca5894f3bce87d3f against the real 64 GiB pair, while t1-vtimer correctly records 'absent'. Nine defects were found by running the queue rather than by reasoning about it, including a cancel that recorded the request and then waited for the job it had cancelled. Evidence: docs/testing/apple-silicon-live-gates.md.

criteria.title: Claim consistency
criteria.statement: README, STATUS, core descriptors, CLI and app wording are generated from or checked against this registry, and a deterministic check fails on drift.
criteria.measured: README and STATUS carry generated blocks rendered from this registry and never hand-edited; render-capability-status.py --check fails on any drift between them. The forbidden-claim scan covers whole trees (crates/**/*.rs excluding /target/, apps/macos/Sources/**/*.swift) plus README, STATUS and docs/hvf-windows-engine-strategy.md, replacing a hand-kept six-file list that silently stopped covering anything added or moved. Falsified this session: appending '// Windows beta' to crates/bridgevm-cli/src/main.rs is reported as "retracted claim 'Windows beta' (product state is Engineering Preview, not beta)" and the check fails; it was not caught before the widening. A mechanical promotion guard also refuses to raise product_state while any release-blocking criterion is unproven. Evidence: docs/windows-arm/capability-matrix.md.

criteria.title: Disk safety
criteria.statement: Powered-off snapshot export and restore keep a byte-exact atomic disk plus vars pair under an explicit byte quota.
criteria.measured: All six acceptance items in docs/windows-arm/snapshot-scope-v1.md are proven against the real 64 GiB image. Items 1-4 and 6 by the pair gate (scripts/verify-powered-off-snapshot.sh, tier t1-snapshot): create, verify, clobber and restore reproduce both files byte for byte, and a tampered snapshot is refused before either live file is touched. Item 5 by the restore-boot gate (scripts/verify-snapshot-restore-boots.sh, tier t1-restore-boot, job 20260805-091656-10876-16297, result=pass): a marker written on C: before the snapshot came back after a restore, and a different marker written after the snapshot was gone -- so a restore that did nothing could not have passed. disk_sha256 56b1361282933f2cf3e409604cdc2da81f8c6ad8536de2bdcc472818e204280d and vars_sha256 8cc43bf0a11d8d1d68253069fed42667950a701c2f508a38c69e35b72fca3563 are identical across create, verify and restore. Evidence: docs/windows-arm/evidence/a19-snapshot-pair-20260804.md and docs/windows-arm/evidence/a19-restore-boots-20260805.md.
